simple.meaning: הָמַם (hâmam) appears 16 times in the Hebrew Scriptures as a person-name in the Hebrew text. The occurrence trail connects the name with an offering. The surrounding account also brings the name into death.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Exodus, Deuteronomy, Joshua, Judges, 1 Samuel, and 6 more, beginning at Exodus 14:24. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as offering, death, Egypt, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to הָמַם (H2000) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows הָמַם through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: הָמַם (hâmam) / H2000 is tracked through Exodus 14:24, Exodus 23:27, Deuteronomy 2:15, Deuteronomy 7:23. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

timeline.evidenceText: In the morning watch, Yahweh looked out on the Egyptian army through the pillar of fire and of cloud, and confused the Egyptian army.
I will send my terror before you, and will confuse all the people to whom you come, and I will make all your enemies turn their backs to you.
Moreover Yahweh’s hand was against them, to destroy them from the middle of the camp, until they were consumed.
But Yahweh your God will deliver them up before you, and will confuse them with a great confusion, until they are destroyed.
Yahweh confused them before Israel. He killed them with a great slaughter at Gibeon, and chased them by the way of the ascent of Beth Horon, and struck them to Azekah and to Makkedah.
Yahweh confused Sisera, all his chariots, and all his army, with the edge of the sword before Barak. Sisera abandoned his chariot and fled away on his feet.

As Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Philistines came near to battle against Israel; but Yahweh thundered with a great thunder on that day on the Philistines, and confused them; and they were struck down before Israel.
He sent out arrows, and scattered them;
He sent out arrows, and scattered them;
They were broken in pieces, nation against nation, and city against city; for God troubled them with all adversity.
because Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast “Pur”, that is the lot, to consume them, and to destroy them;
Then the channels of waters appeared.
Throw out lightning, and scatter them.
Bread flour must be ground; so he will not always be threshing it. Although he drives the wheel of his threshing cart over it, his horses don’t grind it.
“Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon has devoured me.

definitions.full: H2000. hamam הָמַם verb make a noise, move noisily, confuse, discomfit (compare [ הום ]) — Qal Perfect וְהָמַם consecutive Isa 28:28 ; suffix הֲמָמַ֫נִי Jer 51:34 Qr (Kt הֲמָמָ֫נוּ ), הֲמָמָם 2Chr 15:6 ; 1 singular וְהַמֹּתִ֫י Exod 23:27 ; Imperfect וַיָּ֫הָם 14:24 ; Judg 4:15 ; suffix וַיְּהֻמֵּם Josh 10:10 ; 1Sam 7:10 ; Psa 18:15 + 2Sam 22:15 Kt (doubtless right; Qr וַיָּהֹ֑ם ); 2 masculine singular suffix וּתְהֻמֵּם Psa 144:6 ; Infinitive suffix לְהֻמָּם Deut 2:15 ; Est 9:24 ; — 1 move noisily , transitive, drive a wagon in threshing ׳ה וּפָרָשָׁיו עֶגְּלָתוֺ גִּלְגַּל Isa 28:28 (|| דושׁ ). 2 confuse, discomfit , with accusative Exod 14:24 ; 23:27 ; Josh 10:10 ; Judg 4:15 ; 1Sam 7:10 ; Psa 18:15 = 2Sam 22:15 (|| הפיץ ), Psa 144:6 (|| id. ); discomfit, vex , 2Chr 15:6 with accusative & בְּכָלצָֿרָה of instrumental; with accusative also Deut 2:15 (followed by תֻּמָּם עַד ), Est 9:24 (followed by לְאַבְּדָם ); probably also Jer 51:34 (|| אָכַל ), compare הוּם Deut 7:23 .
